evidence.reason: AE-08 phase 8 step 9g: an instrument replaced (another kind or another instance), the parameters of an effect the live path does not take (when the effect keeps its id, kind and delay), and a Granular sample change are adopted at a seam (class 5). withSeamContentOf now takes the instrument of each track and the parameters of the kept, delay-unchanged effects from the installed snapshot, so the adoption comparison no longer needs withLiveContentOf for them. Timeline.tsx's applyPortableProcessor and onStructuralPlaybackChange leave a prepared browser session to the hook's follow. Ledger 444 mutants (p1-controller, p1-audiosync): the materialized Timeline edits are re-anchored to the new guard text (the guard still moves before the bridge error, and the arm is still killed by 'P1 a Synth portable bridge error is still reported and never rebuilds'). Ledger 490 mutants (b6f5, portable, matrix) remove withLiveContentOf from the adoption comparison: they are still killed (11, 40 and 8 failures) but no longer by the live-Synth and non-live instrument witnesses, because the seam content now equals the installed instrument; their recorded fails and counts are re-measured. Ledger 481 mutant matrix: the 'B6F5PROBE ... pending-warm-play proc-nonlive' cells no longer fail (a non-live processor edit is adopted, not rebuilt); the 'structural' cells still kill it. Not re-pointed, reported to the parent: ledger 479 mutants b6f5, matrix and playback (rebuild guard 'rebuildPromise && rebuildInProgress') survive. Their only killer was the 'proc-nonlive' cell of 'B6f5 C', where the Timeline's own late rebuild request landed in the window between rebuildInProgress=false and the promise being cleared; a prepared session no longer asks for that rebuild. See PHASE8-STEP9G.md. Ledger 490 controls (b6f5, portable) record their new pass counts (27 and 160): the witness files gained tests.
